what: The state of the Atlantis case in one small file, made by build/make-case.mjs from plato.json, searches.json and hypotheses.json.

claims.label: The island lay in the Atlantic, in front of the strait the Greeks call the Pillars of Heracles.
claims.quote: for in front of the mouth which you Greeks call, as you say, 'the pillars of Heracles,' there lay an island
claims.how_to_test: Only a direction and a neighbour, not a distance. Any proposed site can be checked against it: is it in the open ocean outside the strait? The sea-floor and shoreline layers answer that (sea-floor depth grids (emodnet-bathymetry-multicolour, srtm15-plus, gmrt-point-and-grid, gebco-wms) and, where a survey exists, noaa-ncei-multibeam-mosaic).

claims.label: At that time the ocean beyond the strait could be sailed.
claims.quote: This power came forth out of the Atlantic Ocean, for in those days the Atlantic was navigable

claims.label: The island was larger than Libya and Asia together.
claims.quote: there lay an island which was larger than Libya and Asia together
claims.how_to_test: A landmass of that size would have to show as a continental shelf or plateau in the Atlantic that was dry at some past sea level. Compare sea-floor depth grids (emodnet-bathymetry-multicolour, srtm15-plus, gmrt-point-and-grid, gebco-wms) and, where a survey exists, noaa-ncei-multibeam-mosaic with the lowered-sea slider (the globe's presets go to -134 m). Nothing is run here; this is the test, not its result.

claims.label: From the island one could pass to other islands, and from them to the whole continent on the far side of the true ocean.
claims.quote: it was possible for the travellers of that time to cross from it to the other islands, and from the islands to the whole of the continent over against them which encompasses that veritable ocean
claims.how_to_test: Plato names no island and gives no distance. A chain of islands leading to a far continent would show as shallow ridges on sea-floor depth grids (emodnet-bathymetry-multicolour, srtm15-plus, gmrt-point-and-grid, gebco-wms) and, where a survey exists, noaa-ncei-multibeam-mosaic; the claim fits any ocean crossing, so it cannot pick a site on its own.

claims.label: The sea inside the strait is only a harbour with a narrow entrance; the outer sea is the real ocean, and the land around it a true continent.
claims.quote: for this sea which is within the Straits of Heracles is only a harbour, having a narrow entrance, but that other is a real sea, and the surrounding land may be most truly called a boundless continent

claims.label: The twin of Atlas, Gadeirus, got the far end of the island toward the Pillars of Heracles, in the region now called Gadeira.
claims.quote: who had for his portion the extremity of the island near the pillars of Heracles up to the part of the country now called Gadeira after the name of that region, was Eumelus in Greek, but in the native tongue Gadeirus
claims.how_to_test: If the island reached or faced the Gadeira coast, a site close to the Gulf of Cádiz fits and one far from it does not. A map test only (sea-floor depth grids (emodnet-bathymetry-multicolour, srtm15-plus, gmrt-point-and-grid, gebco-wms) and, where a survey exists, noaa-ncei-multibeam-mosaic).

claims.label: The island and the Atlantic sea were both named after Atlas, the first king.
claims.quote: the eldest, who was the first king, he named Atlas, and after him the whole island and the ocean were called Atlantic

claims.label: The war with Athens and the sinking happened 9,000 years before the time of the telling.
claims.quote: Of the citizens, then, who lived 9000 years ago, I will declare to you briefly certain of their laws and the noblest of the deeds they performed
claims.how_to_test: A date, so it can be set against the past-world record: sea level, ice and climate at about 9600 BCE (the world-9600bce lane), and any dated sediment layer or tsunami deposit near a proposed site (cores, open-context).

numbers.what: years from the war to the priest's speech to Solon (Athens' citizens of that age)
years from the war to Critias' present, as Critias says it

claims.label: The speakers say the story is true, not an invented tale.
claims.quote: a tale which, though passing strange, is yet wholly true, as Solon, the wisest of the Seven, once upon a time declared

claims.label: Critias says he will treat the ideal city Socrates described yesterday as the ancient Athens of the priest's story.
claims.quote: And the city with its citizens which you described to us yesterday, as it were in a fable, we will now transport hither into the realm of fact

claims.label: Solon found the Egyptian names had been translated into Egyptian, and rendered each into Greek; the writings were kept in Critias' family.
claims.quote: those Egyptians who had first written them down had translated them into their own tongue. So he himself in turn recovered the original sense of each name and, rendering it into our tongue, wrote it down so

claims.label: Atlantis ruled Libya as far as Egypt and Europe as far as Tyrrhenia.
claims.quote: Now in this island of Atlantis there existed a confederation of kings, of great and marvellous power, which held sway over all the island, and over many other islands also and parts of the continent; and, moreover, of the lands here within the Straits they ruled over Libya as far as Egypt , and over Europe as far as Tuscany .

claims.label: The Atlantean power, gathered into one, tried to enslave Europe and Asia inside the strait, and Athens defeated it.
claims.quote: This vast power, gathered into one, endeavoured to subdue at a blow our country and yours and the whole of the region within the straits … she defeated and triumphed over the invaders

claims.short: Sank in a day and a night
claims.label: Violent earthquakes and floods came; in one grievous day and night the Athenian warriors were swallowed by the earth and the island sank under the sea.
claims.quote: But at a later time there occurred portentous earthquakes and floods, and one grievous day and night befell them
claims.how_to_test: A sudden drowning leaves a dated event layer: a tsunami deposit or turbidite in cores, a collapse scar or fault scarp in sea-floor depth grids (emodnet-bathymetry-multicolour, srtm15-plus, gmrt-point-and-grid, gebco-wms) and, where a survey exists, noaa-ncei-multibeam-mosaic, and an earthquake source in plate-boundaries-pb2002 and usgs-earthquakes-geojson. The text says "island", so the trace must be on the sea floor, not a coastal plain.

claims.short: A shoal of mud left behind
claims.label: The sea at that spot is now impassable and unsearchable because of a shoal of mud left by the sinking island.
claims.quote: wherefore also the ocean at that spot has now become impassable and unsearchable, being blocked up by the shoal mud which the island created as it settled down
claims.how_to_test: A broad, shallow fine-sediment bank in the open Atlantic near the strait, shallow enough to stop ships. It is a claim about Plato's own day, not 9600 BCE. Check sea-floor depth grids (emodnet-bathymetry-multicolour, srtm15-plus, gmrt-point-and-grid, gebco-wms) and, where a survey exists, noaa-ncei-multibeam-mosaic; sediment maps and cores would be needed to tell mud from rock.

claims.label: The Egyptian priest says mankind is destroyed again and again, mostly by fire and by water, and that Egypt is spared by the Nile.
claims.quote: There have been, and will be again, many destructions of mankind arising out of many causes; the greatest have been brought about by the agencies of fire and water

claims.label: Critias says many great deluges in the 9,000 years since stripped Attica to "the bones of a sick man".
claims.quote: since many great convulsions took place during the 9000 years—for such was the number of years from that time to this
claims.how_to_test: This is about Athens, not Atlantis. It is the one place where Plato makes a claim about the landscape of the 9,000 years in between. Attic soil and valley-fill records would show whether the land lost soil in big episodes; not something the globe can draw.

claims.short: The hill the rings were cut from
claims.label: Poseidon married Cleito, the only daughter of the native Evenor, and walled her hill with rings; the hill stood about 50 stades from the plain's centre.
claims.quote: Bordering on the sea and extending through the center of the whole island there was a plain, which is said to have been the fairest of all plains and highly fertile; and, moreover, near the plain, over against its center, at a distance of about 50 stades, there stood a mountain that was low on all sides.
claims.how_to_test: A low natural hill about 50 stades (about 9 km at 185 m) from the middle of a large plain, with the sea on one side of the plain. Terrain from copernicus-dem-aws or aws-terrain-tiles-terrarium shows it today; if the site is now under water, sea-floor depth grids (emodnet-bathymetry-multicolour, srtm15-plus, gmrt-point-and-grid, gebco-wms) and, where a survey exists, noaa-ncei-multibeam-mosaic.

numbers.what: distance from the plain to the hill

claims.label: Poseidon cut the hill into rings: three of sea and two of land, alternating and equally spaced, so that nobody could cross.
claims.quote: he made circular belts of sea and land enclosing one another alternately, some greater, some smaller, two being of land and three of sea, which he carved as it were out of the midst of the island
claims.how_to_test: Concentric, near-circular, equally spaced rings around a low hill: about 5.0 km across the outer water ring at 185 m a stade, up to about 23 km across the outer wall. This is the first thing lidar, radar and the bare-earth view (aws-terrain-tiles-terrarium, copernicus-dem-aws, eox-s2cloudless-2016, nasa-gibs-opera-sentinel1-rtc) and sea-floor sonar (sea-floor depth grids (emodnet-bathymetry-multicolour, srtm15-plus, gmrt-point-and-grid, gebco-wms) and, where a survey exists, noaa-ncei-multibeam-mosaic) would show.

claims.label: Water rings are 3, 2 and 1 stades wide, land rings 3 and 2, around a central island 5 stades across.
claims.quote: The greatest of the circles into which a boring was made for the sea was three stades in breadth, and the circle of land next to it was of equal breadth; and of the second pair of circles that of water was two stades in breadth and that of dry land equal again to the preceding one of water; and the circle which ran round the central island itself was of a stade's breadth.
claims.how_to_test: Measure the ring widths in a candidate and compare the 3:3:2:2:1 pattern, and the 5-stade island, not just "rings". Any site needs radial distances in that ratio: the width of the outer water belt is 60 percent of the island's diameter. High-resolution relief and bathymetry only (sea-floor depth grids (emodnet-bathymetry-multicolour, srtm15-plus, gmrt-point-and-grid, gebco-wms) and, where a survey exists, noaa-ncei-multibeam-mosaic).

numbers.what: outermost ring of water (outermost ring, the harbour ring)
innermost ring of water, around the central island

claims.label: The island with the royal palace was five stades across.
claims.quote: And this island, wherein stood the royal palace, was of five stades in diameter.
claims.how_to_test: About 925 m at 185 m a stade (790 to 1,050 m across the range of stadion lengths). A flat circle of that size inside the innermost ring.

claims.label: A canal 3 plethra wide, 100 feet deep and 50 stades long ran from the sea to the outermost ring, wide enough for the largest ships.
claims.quote: a channel right through to the outermost circle, which was three plethra in breadth, one hundred feet in depth, and fifty stades in length
claims.how_to_test: A straight cut about 9 km long (at 185 m), about 90 m wide and 30 m deep, joining the sea to the outer ring. In sea-floor data a straight, flat-floored trench in sediment, in lidar a straight channel or a line of different soil. Sonar tracks: noaa-ncei-survey-coverage, emodnet-bathymetry-wms.

numbers.what: canal length, sea to outermost ring

claims.label: Bridges one plethron wide crossed the water rings; a roofed channel through each land ring let a single trireme pass.
claims.quote: the bridges … a road towards and from the royal palace
claims.how_to_test: Too small for most global data (about 31 m). Only high-resolution lidar or a site survey would show it, and only if the site is on land today.

claims.label: The rings and the island were enclosed by a stone wall with towers and gates; the walls were coated with brass, tin and orichalcum.
claims.quote: The entire circuit of the wall, which went round the outermost zone, they covered with a coating of brass, and the circuit of the next wall they coated with tin, and the third, which encompassed the citadel, flashed with the red light of orichalcum.
claims.how_to_test: Metal coatings do not survive underwater for long; the test is the stone walls themselves, as straight, regular edges in high-resolution relief.

claims.label: The stone for the buildings was white, black and red, quarried from under the central island and the rings; the quarries became roofed double docks.
claims.quote: The stone which was used in the work they quarried from underneath the centre island, and from underneath the zones, on the outer as well as the inner side. One kind was white, another black, and a third red, and as they quarried, they at the same time hollowed out double docks, having roofs formed out of the native rock.
claims.how_to_test: Three colours of workable rock in one small area, one of them cut from beneath the site itself. Geological maps and the Macrostrat layer (macrostrat-geology) show rock type; colour is not in the data, so this narrows candidates only a little.

claims.label: A wall began at the sea, ran round the whole city at a constant 50 stades from the largest ring, and closed on the mouth of the canal; it was crowded with houses and harbour traffic.
claims.quote: one found a wall which began at the sea and ran round in a circle, at a uniform distance of fifty stades from the largest circle and harbor, and its ends converged at the seaward mouth of the channel
claims.how_to_test: The wall circle has a radius of 63.5 stades from the centre (arithmetic, see dimensions): about 11.7 km at 185 m, a circle some 23.5 km across with the canal meeting it at the coast. A circle of that size is the largest, most visible feature of the city in satellite and elevation data.

numbers.what: distance of the outer wall from the largest ring

claims.label: The temple of Poseidon, on the central island, was a stade long and three plethra wide, covered in silver and gold, with a golden statue of the god in a six-horse chariot.
claims.quote: And the temple of Poseidon himself was a stade in length, three plethra in breadth, and of a height which appeared symmetrical therewith; and there was something of the barbaric in its appearance.
claims.how_to_test: A building about 185 m by 92 m at 185 m a stade (a stade long, three plethra wide). Only an excavation or ground-penetrating survey could show it, and only after the rings are found.

numbers.what: number of Nereids on dolphins round the god's statue

claims.label: There were two springs, one warm and one cold, with baths and a sacred grove.
claims.quote: bringing up from beneath the earth two springs of waters, the one flowing warm from its source, the other cold
claims.how_to_test: A warm spring beside a cold one is a local feature. Volcano and fault layers (smithsonian-gvp-volcanoes, plate-boundaries-pb2002) and geology can say whether a candidate has thermal water; many places do, so this narrows little.

claims.label: The ring islands had temples, gardens and exercise grounds; the larger land ring held a race-course a stade wide running all the way round.
claims.quote: in the centre of the larger of the two there was set apart a race-course of a stadium in width, and in length allowed to extend all round the island, for horses to race in

claims.label: The shipyards were full of triremes; the harbour was crowded night and day; the military levy supplied 1,200 ships.
claims.quote: and four sailors towards the manning of twelve hundred ships

claims.label: The whole region rose high and steep out of the sea.
claims.quote: the whole region rose sheer out of the sea to a great height
claims.how_to_test: A steep coast with high ground behind it, with the plain lying in a recess. Visible as a steep shelf edge in sea-floor depth grids (emodnet-bathymetry-multicolour, srtm15-plus, gmrt-point-and-grid, gebco-wms) and, where a survey exists, noaa-ncei-multibeam-mosaic or as cliffs in the terrain tiles.

claims.label: Beside the city lay a smooth, level, oblong plain, 3,000 stades one way and 2,000 stades inland from the sea at its middle, ringed by mountains that ran down to the sea.
claims.quote: this plain had a level surface and was as a whole rectangular in shape, being 3000 stades long on either side and 2000 stades wide at its center, reckoning upwards from the sea
claims.how_to_test: A plain of about 555 by 370 km at 185 m a stade (470 by 315 km at 157.5 m; 576 by 384 km at 192 m). If it was dry land at a lowered sea, it would show as a vast flat shelf in sea-floor depth grids (emodnet-bathymetry-multicolour, srtm15-plus, gmrt-point-and-grid, gebco-wms) and, where a survey exists, noaa-ncei-multibeam-mosaic. The strongest test of scale in the text.

numbers.what: plain width, inland from the sea at the middle

claims.label: This region faced south and was sheltered from the north; the mountains around it were more numerous and beautiful than any now.
claims.quote: And this region, all along the island, faced towards the South and was sheltered from the Northern blasts.
claims.how_to_test: A south-facing plain with high ground on its north side that blocks the wind: elevation data (copernicus-dem-aws) tells whether a candidate faces south and has mountains behind it.

claims.label: The mountains around the plain held rich villages, streams, lakes and meadows, and much timber.
claims.quote: The surrounding mountains were celebrated for their number and size and beauty, far beyond any which still exist, having in them also many wealthy villages of country folk, and rivers, and lakes, and meadows supplying food enough for every animal, wild or tame, and much wood of various sorts

claims.label: A man-made ditch ran round the whole plain, a stade wide and a plethron (100 feet) deep, 10,000 stades long, collecting the mountain streams and emptying into the sea by the city.
claims.quote: it was dug out to the depth of a plethrum and to a uniform breadth of a stade, and since it was dug round the whole plain its consequent length was 10,000 stades
claims.how_to_test: A ring ditch about 185 m wide and 31 m deep that encloses a rectangle, 1,850 km round at 185 m a stade, running to the sea at the city. It would show in relief and in sea-floor depth as a continuous rectilinear trench; sea-floor depth grids (emodnet-bathymetry-multicolour, srtm15-plus, gmrt-point-and-grid, gebco-wms) and, where a survey exists, noaa-ncei-multibeam-mosaic, aws-terrain-tiles-terrarium.

claims.label: Straight canals about 100 feet wide cut across the plain, 100 stades apart, ran into the ditch on the seaward side and carried timber and crops to the city.
claims.quote: Further inland, likewise, straight canals of a hundred feet in width were cut from it through the plain, and again let off into the ditch leading to the sea: these canals were at intervals of a hundred stadia
claims.how_to_test: A grid of parallel straight channels 100 stades (18.5 km) apart over a plain of 555 by 370 km. The text does not say which direction they run. The best test is satellite and relief data over a candidate plain.

claims.label: The land gave two harvests a year, using winter rain and summer irrigation from the canals.
claims.quote: Twice in the year they gathered the fruits of the earth … in winter having the benefit of the rains of heaven, and in summer the water which the land supplied by introducing streams from the canals
claims.how_to_test: A climate with winter rain and a dry summer needing irrigation (a Mediterranean-type climate). It excludes a rain-all-year or a rainless site. Climate reconstruction for 9600 BCE belongs to the world-9600bce lane.

claims.label: The island supplied timber and plenty of tame and wild animals.
claims.quote: There was an abundance of wood for carpenter's work, and sufficient maintenance for tame and wild animals.

claims.label: There were very many elephants on the island, with food for every other animal.
claims.quote: Moreover, it contained a very large stock of elephants
claims.how_to_test: Elephant or proboscidean remains of the right age at a site: a fossil record question (open-context or museum data), not a map. Not a map layer.

claims.label: The island yielded every kind of metal, including orichalcum, which was dug in many places and was the most precious metal after gold.
claims.quote: that which is now only a name and was then something more than a name, orichalcum, was dug out of the earth in many parts of the island, being more precious in those days than anything except gold
claims.how_to_test: Ore districts with copper, tin, silver and gold in one place (macrostrat-geology). The metal "orichalcum" cannot be tested, because it is not identified.

claims.label: Scented plants, cultivated grains and pulses, tree fruits and orchard fruits all grew in great variety.
claims.quote: Also whatever fragrant things there now are in the earth, whether roots, or herbage, or woods, or essences which distil from fruit and flower, grew and thrived in that land

claims.label: Ten kings, descended from Poseidon and Cleito through five pairs of twin sons, each ruled a tenth of the island; Atlas, the eldest, was the overlord.
claims.quote: dividing the island of Atlantis into ten portions, he gave to the first-born of the eldest pair his mother's dwelling and the surrounding allotment, which was the largest and best, and made him king over the rest

numbers.what: kings, and districts of the island

claims.label: Every fifth and sixth year the ten kings met at the temple, hunted bulls with staves and nooses, and cut the throat of one over the orichalcum pillar of laws.
claims.quote: There were bulls who had the range of the temple of Poseidon; and the ten kings, being left alone in the temple, after they had offered prayers to the god that they might capture the victim which was acceptable to him, hunted the bulls, without weapons, but with staves and nooses; and the bull which they caught they led up to the pillar and cut its throat over the top of it so that the blood fell upon the sacred inscription.

claims.label: The plain was split into 60,000 allotments of 10 by 10 stades; the royal city's levy was 10,000 chariots and 1,200 ships.
claims.quote: the size of the allotment was about ten times ten stades, and the total number of all the allotments was 60,000

numbers.what: war-chariots (one sixth of a chariot per allotment)

claims.label: The Critias ends as Zeus calls the gods together to punish the decayed kings; Plato gives no account of the war or the sinking there.
claims.quote: and when he had assembled them, he spake thus:

sank-in-a-day-and-night.how: The BBC reports new evidence that Crete was hit by a massive tsunami at the same time Minoan culture disappeared; proponents read that as the sudden loss Plato describes.

nine-thousand-years.how: The eruption is dated to about 1600 BCE, roughly a thousand years before Solon, not 9,000. Robert Ballard says he does not think Santorini was Atlantis because the eruption date does not match Plato's.

beyond-pillars.how: Santorini is in the Aegean, inside the Mediterranean, not in front of the Pillars of Heracles (our legends.json 'against' note).

santorini.reason: It is the real event most often named as a possible seed of the story, taken seriously by some classicists and archaeologists, while most scholars still read the dialogues as invented (National Geographic).

beyond-pillars.how: Crete lies inside the Mediterranean and never sank (our legends.json 'against' note).

nine-thousand-years.how: Minoan civilisation is a Bronze Age culture, and the eruption that hit it is dated about 1600 BCE (Wikipedia, Minoan eruption), nowhere near 9,600 BCE.

crete.reason: Treated as a possible source of the story's atmosphere by some classicists, never as a location; most scholars take the story as Plato's invention (National Geographic).

sank-in-a-day-and-night.how: A winter night, an earthquake and a tidal wave.

beyond-pillars.how: Helike was on the Gulf of Corinth, inside Greece (our legends.json 'against' note).

larger-than-libya-and-asia.how: Helike was one Greek city (our legends.json 'against' note).

helike.reason: The destruction is well documented and the Helike Project and the BBC present it as the likely seed; this is the view of those researchers, not a consensus among classicists.

beyond-pillars.how: Spartel is just outside the Strait of Gibraltar, on the Atlantic side.

nine-thousand-years.how: Sea-level rise drowned the island's top about 11,600 years ago, close to Plato's 9,000 years before Solon.

sank-in-a-day-and-night.how: Gutscher tested whether a great earthquake and tsunami like Lisbon 1755 could have destroyed it.

larger-than-libya-and-asia.how: The mapped island is small; Gutscher estimated it at less than 500 m across at the time of the drowning (as reported in a 2005 Nature news piece reposted on Free Republic; original not fetched).

ringed-city.how: The same report says Gutscher's survey showed no unusual geometric structures; Wikipedia adds that in follow-up correspondence he said the island could not have supported the Bronze Age society Plato describes.

spartel-bank.reason: The island is real, but its main geological analyst (Gutscher) and the classicist reviewer (Nesselrath) both say it is not Plato's Atlantis.

beyond-pillars.how: The marsh is just outside the Strait of Gibraltar on the Atlantic coast.

ringed-city.how: Kühne: 'We have in the photos concentric rings just as Plato described.' He says the rings are slightly larger than Plato's figures and offers a longer stade as the explanation.

great-plain.how: The plain from the south coast to Seville, with the Sierra Morena and Sierra Nevada as the mountains (Kühne).

orichalcum-and-metals.how: Copper is abundant in the Sierra Morena mines (Kühne).

nine-thousand-years.how: Kühne dates the flood to 800 to 500 BCE, and the Sea Peoples war to about 1200 BCE, not 9,600 BCE (Colavito also notes the mismatch).

larger-than-libya-and-asia.how: Plato's island was larger than Libya and Asia together; the Spanish site is far smaller (Colavito).

donana.reason: Argued by a few researchers and television producers; the Spanish archaeologists working on the site and independent remote-sensing experts did not accept the rings as a city.

ringed-city.how: Promoters note concentric rings; the structure has three nested rings by Matton et al.'s description (a geological fact, not a claim of Atlantis).

beyond-pillars.how: It lies deep in the Sahara, inland from the Atlantic coast, not in front of the Pillars (our legends.json 'against' note).

ringed-city.how: The rings are rock ridges eroded from a dome; there is no sign of dug canals or a built city, and no midden or buildings were found (Wikipedia, Richat Structure).

richat.reason: Promoted outside scholarship; geology and archaeology done for other reasons exclude a built city, but nobody has tested the Atlantis claim directly.

red-white-black-stone.how: Donnelly: 'upon the Azores black lava rocks, and rocks red and white in color, are now found.'

hot-and-cold-springs.how: Donnelly: 'hot springs abound in the Azores, which are the surviving fragments of Atlantis.'

mountains-shelter-north.how: Donnelly: the surrounding mountains 'are represented in the present towering peaks of the Azores.'

beyond-pillars.how: The Azores lie in the open Atlantic, about 1,400 km west of Portugal.

nine-thousand-years.how: Cores show the Azores plateau has been under water for millions of years; relict beaches show the islands have not subsided (Wikipedia summary of the geology).

azores.reason: Examined by geologists a century ago and since; the sea floor has been deep for millions of years.

nine-thousand-years.how: Radiocarbon dates on the blocks' shells and cement are 2,770 to 3,510 years before present, not 11,600; and the blocks are beachrock (Wikipedia, citing Calvert and others 1979).

bimini-road.reason: Cores and dates by USGS and university geologists show a natural formation, and the claim is not defended in scholarship.

nine-thousand-years.how: Hapgood's pole shift is dated about 9,600 BCE, matching Plato's date.

beyond-pillars.how: Antarctica is not in front of the Pillars of Heracles; the Flem-Aths and Hancock argue the crust moved so that the old Atlantic position is now the pole (our reading of Wikipedia).

antarctica.reason: Geophysics replaced crustal slip, and ice cores show continuous ice; this is the view of earth scientists, not of Atlantis writers.

sank-in-a-day-and-night.how: He describes a catastrophic loss of land in the Bronze Age and calls Heligoland's royal island 'Basileia'.

elephants.how: Atlantipedia says Spanuth could not reconcile Heligoland with Plato's elephants.

nine-thousand-years.how: His date is 1200 BCE, not 9,600 BCE.

heligoland.reason: Archaeologists did not accept the claim and Spanuth had to fight critics in court (Atlantipedia); no Bronze Age city has been found there.

beyond-pillars.how: Sweden is not in front of the Pillars; Rudbeck's case rested on matching names and local pride (our legends.json 'against' note).

gamla-uppsala.reason: A 17th-century patriotic reading, long set aside by scholars; no one now defends it.

beyond-pillars.how: Ireland lies in the Atlantic; 'geography and landscape ... match Ireland almost exactly' (Erlingsson).

sank-in-a-day-and-night.how: Ireland did not sink; Erlingsson places the sinking at Dogger Bank (our legends.json note).

ireland.reason: Argued in one book by a geographer; no archaeologists or classicists have taken it up in the sources I found.

ringed-city.how: Sarmast: 'their location and lengths match exactly the description of the acropolis of Atlantis provided by Plato.'

beyond-pillars.how: It lies in the eastern Mediterranean, not in front of the Pillars.

nine-thousand-years.how: Sediment cores from the basin show it has been under water for millions of years (Wikipedia summary of ODP Leg 160).

cyprus-basin.reason: Marine geologists who had surveyed the same seabed say the shapes are natural folds, and the basin has been deep for millions of years.

beyond-pillars.how: If the Pillars are the Strait of Sicily, Sardinia is beyond them.

sank-in-a-day-and-night.how: A comet-driven tidal wave struck Bronze Age settlements (scientists quoted by The Guardian, including geophysicist Stefano Tinti).

nine-thousand-years.how: The proposed disaster is about 1175 BCE.

sardinia.reason: Rests on moving the Pillars, which most scholars reject; an interdisciplinary Italian team was reported but no peer-reviewed support is cited.

war-with-athens.how: A Greek civilisation fights a mighty power abroad: Mycenaean Greece against Troy.

sank-in-a-day-and-night.how: Torrential flood and major earthquake at Tiryns at the end of the Bronze Age.

beyond-pillars.how: Troy is in the eastern Aegean; Zangger treats the Pillars and location as distortion.

troy.reason: Published in a journal but not taken up by classicists; Zangger himself later withdrew from academia after a dispute with the Troy excavator (Wikipedia).

beyond-pillars.how: Atlantipedia notes Scranton was 'somewhat unsettled' that Plato puts Atlantis to the west of Athens and Egypt, not in Boeotia.

nine-thousand-years.how: The first drainage works date to the 14th century BCE (Wikipedia, Lake Copais).

lake-copais.reason: A one-off proposal in a magazine article; the drainage works are real but the match to Plato's text has not been taken up by classicists or archaeologists in sources I found.

malta.reason: Argued by Maltese authors and amateurs, not by classicists; the earliest 'evidence' was a documented forgery.

sank-in-a-day-and-night.how: Tantalis was said in Greek tradition to have been destroyed by an earthquake.

beyond-pillars.how: James moves the origin of the story to Lydia and treats Plato's Egypt and Atlantic setting as a mistake (Atlantipedia).

tantalis-sipylus.reason: A trade book that reviews and rejects earlier theories; I found no published scholarly reply or field test.

great-plain.how: A huge plain flooded when the barrier at the Bosporus broke.

sank-in-a-day-and-night.how: Sudden flooding after the Bosporus breach.

nine-thousand-years.how: Their date is about 5500 BCE, not 9,600 BCE.

fleet-and-harbours.how: Wikipedia notes they do not explain how merchant ships reached a harbour about 350 ft below global sea level.

beyond-pillars.how: Redefines the Pillars as the Bosporus; Atlantipedia's editor notes Plato says the attackers came from the Atlantic.

black-sea.reason: Argued by two amateur researchers; their website is reported gone and the underlying flood hypothesis itself is contested.

nine-thousand-years.how: The proposed event is dated 9,600 BCE.

great-plain.how: The Sea of Azov is said to have been the irrigated plain beside the city.

beyond-pillars.how: It is far east of the Strait of Gibraltar.

sea-of-azov.reason: Promoted in a self-published book; no scholar in the sources I found has taken it up.

red-white-black-stone.how: Rocks coloured red, white and black still in use in buildings in the same area (Atlantipedia's description of his videos).

fleet-and-harbours.how: Possible harbour remains close to Cape Ghir.

beyond-pillars.how: The plain lies on the Atlantic coast of Morocco, south of the Strait.

empire-to-egypt-and-tyrrhenia.how: Atlantipedia's editor says Agadir is about 3,300 km by sea from Athens, too far for the Atlantean war, and that Plato says the empire reached Tyrrhenia, not lay west of it.

souss-massa.reason: Argued by an independent researcher at the Athens conference and in a German book; praised for method by some Atlantis writers but without field verification.

beyond-pillars.how: Morocco has an Atlantic coast just outside the Strait, and Herodotus calls its inhabitants Atalantes.

atlas-morocco.reason: A 19th-century reading revived by modern writers; Atlantipedia says it had little support beyond the 1920s, and I found no field test.

beyond-pillars.how: On the Atlantic coast of Morocco.

sale-chellah.reason: Presented at an Atlantis conference; no archaeology targeted at the claim and the site is a Phoenician and Roman city, not a sunken one.

elephants.how: (Atlantipedia's editor, not Herrmann or Borchardt) Atlantipedia notes Tunisia held the last wild elephants of the Mediterranean region until the Roman Empire ended (citing New Scientist, 1985).

two-harvests.how: (Atlantipedia's editor, not Herrmann or Borchardt) Two crops a year can be grown in the irrigated Tunisian lowlands.

ringed-city.how: Herrmann reduced Plato's dimensions by a factor of 30, claiming the Egyptian priest erred converting schoinoi into stades.

nine-thousand-years.how: Herrmann read 9,000 as the 13th or 14th century BCE.

tunisian-chotts.reason: An early 20th-century school of French and German writers, revived by a few modern authors; it needs Plato's numbers and the date to be changed.

beyond-pillars.how: The Hoggar is deep inland in the central Sahara, not in front of the Pillars. Atlantipedia's entry shows a map placing Atlantis in the Atlantic to the west.

hoggar-sahara.reason: A 1920s explorer's belief with a failed supporting claim; no modern scholarship defends it.

nigeria-ife.reason: A diffusionist reading from the early 20th century that treats the story as a memory of Yoruba culture; no modern scholarship in the sources I found defends it.

sank-in-a-day-and-night.how: The researcher says: 'They were islands in the past and they have sunk, they are still sinking, as the legend of Atlantis tells.'

nine-thousand-years.how: The islands existed 56 to 34 million years ago (Eocene), long before people.

los-atlantes.reason: The Atlantis remark is a press comment by one lead researcher about a seamount that sank millions of years before humans; the geology itself is ordinary.

beyond-pillars.how: It lies in the Atlantic, off north Spain.

nine-thousand-years.how: Wikipedia says detailed geological studies show the bank has been submerged for millions of years; the studies are not named there.

le-danois-bank.reason: One author's book; geology as summarised by Wikipedia argues against it.

great-plain.how: A low-lying plain, now under the Irish Sea.

nine-thousand-years.how: His date for the catastrophe is about 3100 BCE (Wikipedia).

irish-sea.reason: A trade-press book, rejected by the sources I found as pseudo-science; no sea-floor survey was done to test it.

beyond-pillars.how: In the Atlantic, off the south-west tip of Britain.

little-sole-bank.reason: A press-reported claim never surveyed; Atlantipedia notes the institute he named is doubtful.

sank-in-a-day-and-night.how: Doggerland was flooded; a tsunami from the Storegga Slide about 8,200 years ago hit its coast.

nine-thousand-years.how: The flooding is dated about 6200 BCE, not 9,600 BCE.

ringed-city.how: Silverpit crater is a 45 to 74 million-year-old structure whose impact origin is disputed, not a built city.

dogger-bank.reason: The flooded Doggerland is real archaeology; tying it to Plato rests on one book.

islands-and-opposite-continent.how: Plato's far continent was read as the newly found land, reached by a route through the island.

beyond-pillars.how: America lies west of the Strait across the Atlantic.

sank-in-a-day-and-night.how: America did not sink; Bacon himself calls Plato's description 'poetical and fabulous' while keeping a core of truth.

americas-early-modern.reason: A Renaissance identification long set aside by modern scholarship, which treats Plato's island as sunk, and America as inhabited and unsunk.

nine-thousand-years.how: The Cuban geologist Manuel Iturralde said it would have taken about 50,000 years for such structures to sink to that depth, when no culture could build complex buildings.

cuba-guanahacabibes.reason: The sonar finding is real but unexplained; the Atlantis link came from press coverage, not from the surveyors' own claim, and no follow-up work is reported.

plain-ditch.how: A vast canal network in the region.

ringed-city.how: Aerial photography indicating concentric rings on the ground.

red-white-black-stone.how: Pampa Aullagas contains red, white and black rock.

empire-to-egypt-and-tyrrhenia.how: Atlantipedia notes it conflicts with Plato's dating, dimensions, and the improbability of an invasion of the eastern Mediterranean from the west coast of South America.

beyond-pillars.how: The Andes are an ocean away from the Pillars.

bolivian-altiplano.reason: Self-promoted by one author with a critique from an independent writer; archaeologists have not examined it as an Atlantis site.

yucatan-maya.reason: The decipherments failed and the Maya script was later read as a record of Maya language and history; this is the verdict of epigraphers and of the reference sources above.

nine-thousand-years.how: Sundaland's shelf was dry land during the ice age and drowned as the ice melted (Atlantipedia on Indonesia).

beyond-pillars.how: Santos redefines the Pillars of Heracles as the Krakatau and Dempo mountains in the Sunda Strait, against the Greek-usage of Gibraltar.

sundaland.reason: Promoted by Santos's followers and a few Indonesian scientists; no classicists or archaeologists in the sources I found endorse it.

elephants.how: Bailly proposed the Arctic once had a warmer climate, to allow large animals.

beyond-pillars.how: Spitsbergen is not in front of the Pillars.

arctic-spitsbergen.reason: An 18th-century reading overtaken by later climate and ice-core science; no modern scholar defends it.

beyond-pillars.how: The Levant is at the eastern end of the Mediterranean.

holy-land.reason: A Bible-based reading abandoned by scholars in the 18th century; the modern version is argued outside scholarship.

ten-kings.how: Cádiz is accepted as ancient Gades, considered the kingdom of Gadeirus, twin brother of Atlas.

cadiz-gades.reason: The place-name link is old, but the 1973 expedition found nothing verifiable; this is Atlantipedia's account.

beyond-pillars.how: Atlantipedia notes Kircher's map places Atlantis between the Strait of Gibraltar and America, not between Canada and Scandinavia.

greenland.reason: A few authors compare maps; no field or survey work is cited.

searches.title: Olof Rudbeck's Atlantica: Sweden as Atlantis
searches.who: Olof Rudbeck (Olaus Rudbeck the Elder), professor of medicine at Uppsala
searches.announced: A four-volume, 3,000-page treatise argued that Sweden was Atlantis, the cradle of civilization, and that Swedish was the original language of Adam.
searches.outcome: The argument was made from texts, so nobody ran a physical test. It was criticised by contemporaries, including the Danish professor Ludvig Holberg.

searches.title: Ignatius Donnelly, Atlantis: The Antediluvian World
searches.announced: Atlantis was real, was a large island in the Atlantic and the source of all later civilizations, and the Azores are its remnant.
searches.outcome: Swedish oceanographer Hans Pettersson argued in 1944 that no island in the Atlantic could have sunk in the time Plato gives, because continents do not sink and the Mid-Atlantic Ridge is building volcanic crust. Plate tectonics later became accepted.

searches.title: Termier's Atlantis lecture and the Azores lava glass
searches.announced: Termier argued the tachylite could only have cooled to glass in air, so the sea floor it came from was land not more than about 25,000 years ago.
searches.outcome: Högbom said in 1938 that lava can cool to glass under water, and that rocks rafted by Ice Age icebergs to the Azores all settled near today's coast, which means land and sea levels there have been about the same since the last Ice Age. Pettersson adopted…

searches.title: K. T. Frost: the Critias and Minoan Crete
searches.announced: Plato's Atlantis story is best understood as a memory of Minoan Crete. A first version of the idea dates to 1909, according to Colavito.
searches.outcome: The identification is a literary argument, and I found no survey or excavation reported as a test of it as Atlantis. Plato puts the island in the Atlantic and 9,000 years before Solon, which Crete does not match.

searches.title: Bigelow and Iselin's Azores cruise on the ketch Atlantis
searches.announced: Newspapers reported that scientists would probe for Atlantis on the cruise; the scientists' stated aim was to study large currents.
searches.outcome: The crew found nothing and made no claim.

searches.title: Marinatos: volcanic destruction of Minoan Crete
searches.announced: The Minoan palace catastrophes on Crete were contemporaneous and caused by the Thera eruption. The abstract does not mention Atlantis.
searches.outcome: The Antiquity editors added a postscript saying the evidence was insufficient for the claim that the eruption destroyed Minoan civilisation, and the hypothesis has since been rejected as stated. The eruption itself is real; Marinatos then dug Akrotiri.

searches.title: Pettersson's geophysical case against an Atlantic Atlantis
searches.announced: No Atlantic land could have sunk in the last ice age or since; continents do not sink, and the Mid-Atlantic Ridge is erupting new crust.
searches.outcome: Franke notes that continental drift was accepted only in the 1960s and 1970s, which supports Pettersson's reasoning. I read no later paper in this lane.

searches.title: Mavor's search for Atlantis off Thera
searches.announced: WHOI says Mavor and colleagues found evidence of a Minoan city, and that the site seemed to mirror Plato's account.
searches.outcome: WHOI says a long dispute over credit left the findings in doubt. The best-documented Minoan town on Thera, Akrotiri, was found by land excavation from 1967 and dated to the 16th to 17th century BCE.

searches.title: Akrotiri excavations on Thera begin
searches.announced: Marinatos's choice of the site paid off within hours: a buried Minoan town with frescoes was found.
searches.outcome: The town is real and was destroyed in the Theran eruption in the 16th century BCE per Wikipedia; radiocarbon work gives 1627 to 1600 BCE. That is about 8,000 years after Plato's date, and the site is inside the Aegean. It confirms a real buried town, not…

searches.title: Bimini Road found; Cayce's Atlantis readings
searches.announced: Divers reported a pavement of rounded stones that they thought might be man-made, which became known as the Bimini Road.
searches.outcome: Geologists who studied it found beachrock jointed into blocks. See the 1977 to 1980 coring and dating entry.

searches.title: Soviet photographs of a 'wall' on Ampère Seamount
searches.announced: Photographs seemed to show cut blocks and steps on the summit, which led to Atlantis speculation. Aksyonov publicised the photos in 1979 and thought the stones had stood on dry land, but did not himself call them Atlantean.
searches.outcome: Atlantipedia says that when better images were obtained, Aksyonov declared the features natural. This rests on a secondary and fringe-friendly site.

searches.title: Cores and dating of the Bimini Road
searches.announced: Proponents held the stones were a worked road or wall. Cores from the stones gave seven radiocarbon ages between 2,750 and 3,510 radiocarbon years BP, on whole rock, shells and cement, and the stones are beachrock.
searches.outcome: The published consensus is natural beachrock broken by joints. Proponents argued the dates came from whole-rock samples open to young carbon; Wikipedia says the background data show not all were whole-rock.

searches.title: Sonar images of structures off western Cuba (ADC survey)
searches.announced: The company said it had found stone structures that might be a drowned city. Zelitsky declined to name them until there was evidence, and did not link them to Atlantis.
searches.outcome: Experts quoted at the time were cautious and no published follow-up survey was found in the 2014 summary I read. Critics noted the depth, about 650 m, is far below any Ice Age sea level.

searches.title: Collina-Girard proposes Spartel Bank
searches.announced: At the ice-age low a 14 by 5 km island stood off Cape Spartel, in a sheltered sea 77 km long. The rising sea drowned it for good about 11,300 years ago.
searches.outcome: A Bryn Mawr Classical Review (2009) of his book found real prehistory but not Atlantis. Gutscher, who mapped the bank, later said it could not have supported Plato's Bronze Age society.

searches.title: Gutscher's survey and earthquake test of the Spartel Bank
searches.announced: A great earthquake and tsunami like 1755 could explain a sudden sinking about 11,600 years ago, and an unusually thick turbidite about 12 ka may fit. The bank's shape and the case for human habitation were reported.
searches.outcome: In follow-up correspondence Gutscher said the island could not have been Atlantis, since Spartel could not have supported the Bronze Age society Plato describes.

searches.title: Kühne and Wickboldt: rings in satellite photos of the Doñana marshes
searches.announced: Satellite photos of the Marisma de Hinojos show two rectangles and parts of concentric rings that Kühne reads as Plato's temples and ring system. Wickboldt first spotted them.
searches.outcome: The Spanish Hinojos Project later worked in the same marsh. It found a settlement about 5,000 years old under metres of sediment, which is a different date from Plato's, but I found no published test of the specific rectangles and rings.

searches.title: Sarmast's expedition and the 'Atlantis' hill off Cyprus
searches.announced: Sarmast said his team had definitely found Atlantis. At the news conference in Limassol he showed only animated simulations of the hill.
searches.outcome: A German geophysicist and others said the feature was a mud volcano or natural salt-tectonic fold. Later published surveys by Hübscher and colleagues described a natural compressional fold and a slide scar.

searches.title: Spanish Hinojos Project in the Doñana marsh
searches.who: CSIC, Universities of Huelva, Granada and Barcelona, FUHEM
searches.announced: The marsh was inhabited about 5,000 years ago by farmers and herders. A marine flood between 2200 and 2000 BCE, coinciding with a Gulf of Cádiz tsunami, ended that community. Further Atlantic tsunamis followed around 1450 BCE and about…
searches.outcome: The release does not mention Atlantis. It dates a real settlement in the marsh to the third millennium BCE, more than 6,000 years after Plato's date. It also says the coast sank progressively until the first centuries CE.

searches.title: Milos conference and the 24 criteria
searches.announced: A list of 24 criteria, including: outside the Pillars of Hercules; alternating concentric rings of land and water; sunk entirely or partly; destroyed 9,000 Egyptian years before the 6th century BCE; elephants present; hot and cold…
searches.outcome: No site has been shown to meet the list. The Atlantipedia author calls its main flaw the assumption that all of Plato's account is factual, and Jim Allen expanded it to 50 points and used it to favour his Bolivian site.

searches.title: Geology of the Richat Structure (Matton et al.)
searches.announced: The structure is a Cretaceous alkaline complex that domed the rocks and was hollowed by hot-water karst, with erosion forming the rings.
searches.outcome: The IUGS listed it in 2022 among 100 geological heritage sites as 'a spectacular example of a magmatic concentric alkaline complex'. This is a geology paper, not an Atlantis test; it sets the age and origin that Atlantis proposals must answer.

searches.title: Radiocarbon dating of the Thera eruption
searches.who: Walter Friedrich and colleagues (Friedrich et al.)
searches.announced: The eruption dates to 1627 to 1600 BCE (95.4% probability), a century before the date from traditional Egyptian chronology. Manning's team put it in the late 17th century BCE.
searches.outcome: The date moved about a century earlier than archaeology had held, but stays about 8,000 years after Plato's. The Egyptian-linked chronology remains debated among archaeologists, per the search summaries I saw; I did not read the debate itself.

searches.title: Atlantis Hypothesis conferences in Athens and Santorini
searches.announced: The series ran as 2005 on Milos, 2008 in Athens, 2011 on Santorini.
searches.outcome: No criteria or finding from these two meetings were fetched. Franke notes he did not attend the 2011 conference and lists reports only in German.

searches.title: Cyprus Basin salt tectonics and mud volcanoes (Hübscher et al.)
searches.announced: Wikipedia cites this 2009 paper for the finding that the features Sarmast read as walls are a natural fold and a slide scar. A German physicist and two colleagues told Cyprus Mail in 2004 they had surveyed the area the year before; I…
searches.outcome: The natural reading has not been contested in anything I found.

searches.title: The 'Atlantis' grid in Google Ocean
searches.announced: A tabloid asked 'Is This Atlantis?' and quoted an aeronautical engineer saying the grid must be man-made.
searches.outcome: Google said the lines were the tracks of a survey ship. In 2012 a data update removed the grid, and Sandwell explained a velocity error on one grid-pattern survey cruise.

searches.title: Freund's 'Finding Atlantis' at Doñana
searches.announced: The team said it found a communal oven and canal systems buried in the park, evidence of a roughly 4,000-year-old civilisation flooded by a tsunami, and suggested the site was Atlantis and also the biblical Tarshish.
searches.outcome: Members of the Spanish team working there since 2005 criticised the claim. Their own results point to a third-millennium BCE settlement. Critics note the dates and size do not fit Plato.

searches.title: 'Atlantis Rising' (James Cameron, Simcha Jacobovici)
searches.announced: Per Colavito: Atlantis might be a real Bronze Age Mediterranean power. The film looked at Thera, Malta, southern Spain and Sardinia, and Jacobovici presented Sardinia as a candidate.
searches.outcome: The film announced no new dated find of its own that I could see. Colavito's published review disputes its method and the fit with Plato.

searches.title: Jimmy Corsetti's Richat video ('Bright Insight')
searches.announced: Per neurologist and sceptic Steven Novella: the Richat's concentric rings match Plato's city, and the Atlanteans built into the natural dome.
searches.outcome: Nobody has reported excavating for a city at the site. The dome's origin is settled geology. Novella notes there is no archaeology of a city there.

searches.title: Merlin Burrows: 'towers' and a sea wall at Doñana
searches.announced: The company said it had found remains of temples and towers and a long sea wall, with material thought to be early concrete dated to 10,000 to 12,000 years. A film titled 'Atlantica' was announced.
searches.outcome: A critic found the oval 'circles' were experimental ponds dug in 2004 to 2005 for a zooplankton study, and that they are absent from older Google Earth imagery. The ponds' construction is confirmed by the published paper.

searches.title: Graham Hancock's 'Ancient Apocalypse' and the SAA letter
searches.announced: Hancock presents a theory that an advanced civilisation was destroyed around 12,000 years ago by meteor impacts. Wikipedia's account of the series does not mention Atlantis in its text.
searches.outcome: The series names no Atlantis site that I could find. The Society for American Archaeology asked Netflix to reclassify it as science fiction; Wikipedia quotes the letter. Some featured archaeologists said their interviews were taken out of context.

searches.title: Cádiz coast 'walls': Chipiona press conference
searches.announced: A team reported large concentric circular structures like walls, resembling Plato's description. Donnellan said the match to Plato was perfect but that the team could not say it was Atlantis.
searches.outcome: The archaeologist called it 'the first data'. A Huelva stratigraphy professor said the coastal formations he has studied show no human action, though he was speaking about the region, not this site.

searches.title: 'Atlantica' film and the Cádiz concentric-wall claim
searches.announced: Donnellan said sonar showed concentric circular walls each 6.096 m high, with a central rectangular ruin he compared to the Temple of Poseidon, and tied the destruction to the Younger Dryas.
searches.outcome: The Jerusalem Post says Donnellan did not convince the scientific community, and he says geologists date the structures to 10,000 to 12,000 years. No published paper or independent survey was found.

searches.title: 'Codex running for 26 days searching for Atlantis' (pash, OpenAI)
searches.announced: pash says an AI agent has searched for Atlantis for 26 days and the best candidate is the Faroe Plateau, but it needs more time. The post gives no data, method, map or repository.
searches.outcome: No write-up, data or follow-up claim was found in pash's replies of that day. pash joked 'heinrich schliemann moment' to one reply and, replying to Polymarket, asked 'okay where's the "Atlantis discovered by ____" market'.
